provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after qui and none after tuae, so it does not fence off the ablative abundantia pietatis tuae; 1862 prints adjicias where the typica prints adicias; 1862 conclusion is the short cue Per Dominum where the typica prints Per Dominum nostrum. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at lines 52523-52530, read there, which agrees with the 1862 in having no comma after qui and prints adijcias; 1604 at line 38180.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui, abundantia pietatis tuae, et merita
supplicum excedis et vota: effunde super nos misericordiam tuam; ut dimittas
quae conscientia metuit, et adjicias quod oratio non praesumit. Per Dominum
nostrum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
